review_scope: Seven owned R2 files downloaded, hashes matched to provenance, FFprobe checked and six evenly spaced frames per video visually inspected. Existing review reports consulted where present. No continuous motion/listening assessment, latency benchmark or current production-image validation. Demonstrated means historical mechanism only.

runtime.supports: Cuts, crops, compositing, captions and audio mixing on supplied media.
runtime.limits: Needs source assets; does not synthesize footage.

runtime.supports: Custom HTML/SVG/Canvas in Chromium with absolute-time animation.
runtime.limits: Local assets and fonts only; no network imports; author and inspect actual motion.

runtime.supports: Programmatic diagrams, geometry, charts, mathematical labels and transitions.
runtime.limits: Installed runtime, not proof of arbitrary illustration or scientific correctness.

runtime.supports: Procedural meshes, local models, camera, materials and authored deformation.
runtime.limits: CPU Chromium; no Blender/CAD, native generative footage, cloth/fluid solver or photoreal guarantee. Current worker WebGL not probed by this audit.

examples.supports: Letterform compression, counters, negative space and staged composition.
examples.limits: 14s silent authored SVG/browser film; revisions needed, not automatic one-shot proof.
examples.prompt: Create a 12–16 second kinetic typography film about the words MAKE ROOM. Make the letterforms themselves compress, negotiate space, and open into a surprising beautifully balanced composition. Invent the choreography and typography. It should feel like an excellent moving graphic-design poster, with a strong visual payoff, not a succession of title cards.

examples.supports: Layered paper/photo cutouts, continuous river path and scale changes.

examples.prompt: Create a 15–20 second wordless editorial collage film about a river finding its way through a city. Use a coherent family of flat paper, print, map and photographic fragments, with tactile edges and surprising scale changes. A continuous visual connection should carry us through three distinct compositions. Invent or source your own permitted assets and keep it a designed collage, not slides with camera pans.

examples.supports: Footage cutdown, portrait crop preserving product/hands and phrase captions.
examples.limits: 13.61s uses existing footage and speech; does not generate actors/products or validate listening.
examples.prompt: Make a useful 12–15 second vertical short from this widescreen camera-unboxing footage. Choose one complete product demonstration with an actual reveal or useful takeaway. Cut the idle handling and pauses, reframe each shot to keep the camera and the demonstrator’s hands visible, and move the crop only when the product moves. Keep any included speech intact and add clean accurate phrase captions within safe margins. Use the speaker’s own voice and real sounds. No blurred background bars, stretching, fake words, music, or decorative transitions.
examples.prompt_provenance: exact creative prompt; technical delivery instructions stored separately
